c.tagline: Portuguese colonial charm beneath dazzling lights.

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the crowded Senado Square–Ruins of St Paul's stretch, and casino areas attract loan-shark and money-changing scams.

hood_desc: The historic core of the city blending Portuguese colonial architecture, temples, and old casinos with dense local life, ideal for heritage sightseeing and travelers wanting authentic Macanese character.
A charming district with a preserved old village of narrow lanes, colonial houses, and renowned Macanese and Portuguese eateries, great for foodies and those seeking old-world atmosphere.
The glitzy reclaimed strip of mega-resorts, casinos, and lavish shows modeled on Las Vegas, suiting luxury seekers, gamblers, and families visiting themed resorts.
A quiet, green, laid-back island retreat with beaches, hiking trails, and the famous Lord Stow's egg tarts, perfect for those wanting to escape the casino crowds and relax.

water.note: Tap water meets WHO standards and is safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buses charge a flat MOP 6 (~US$0.75) — pay exact cash on board or use a Macau Pass card from convenience stores. The LRT sells single-trip tickets from station machines and also takes Macau Pass. Mobile QR payments (MPay, Alipay) work on most buses.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am to midnight with a few overnight N routes; the LRT runs about 6:30am to 11:15pm.
transit.note: Free casino and hotel shuttle buses link the ferry terminals, border crossings, airport and Cotai resorts — many visitors get around mainly on these.

landmarks: Ruins of St. Paul's
The dramatic stone facade of a 17th-century church that survived a fire, now Macau's most iconic postcard image.
Senado Square (Largo do Senado)
A UNESCO-listed plaza with a wave-patterned mosaic pavement and pastel Portuguese colonial buildings.
A-Ma Temple
Macau's oldest temple, over 500 years old, with incense-filled shrines built into a rocky hillside above the harbor.
Macau Tower
A 338-meter observation tower offering panoramic city views and thrill activities like the SkyWalk and bungee jump.
Guia Fortress and Lighthouse
A 17th-century hilltop fort with the oldest Western-style lighthouse on the China coast, framed by sweeping city views.
The Venetian Macao
A vast Venice-themed resort with indoor canals and gondola rides, epitomizing Macau's dazzling casino architecture.
Macau Cathedral (Sé Cathedral)
A grand Portuguese colonial cathedral with stained glass windows, centrally located near Senado Square.
Mandarin's House
A sprawling 19th-century traditional Chinese courtyard residence showcasing Lingnan architecture and history.
Fisherman's Wharf
A themed waterfront entertainment complex blending replica architecture from Europe, Egypt, and Rome for whimsical photos.
Coloane Village
A charming, quiet fishing village with pastel Portuguese-style houses and the picturesque Chapel of St. Francis Xavier.

train.note: Macau has no mainline railway — only the local LRT light metro. For China's high-speed rail network, cross the border on foot at the Border Gate or Hengqin checkpoints to Zhuhai, whose railway station sits right at the Gongbei border.

intl.to: Hong Kong & Zhuhai via the HZMB bridge
Hong Kong (city centre to city centre)

bus.note: The HZMB shuttle ('Golden Bus') runs 24 hours from the Macau Port plaza near the Border Gate; clear immigration on foot, then board the next departure. Long-standing operator Kee Kwan also runs coaches to Guangzhou and other Guangdong cities from the Border Gate. Passport needed for every crossing.

intl.to: Hong Kong (Sheung Wan & HK Airport SkyPier)

ferry.note: TurboJET sails from the Outer Harbour Ferry Terminal on the peninsula; Cotai Water Jet from the Taipa Ferry Terminal near the airport and Cotai casinos. The SkyPier sailings are only for passengers connecting to flights at Hong Kong airport.

half.name: Hong Kong
half.blurb: A short ferry ride away, people go for its skyline, harbour views, shopping and dining.

half.name: Zhuhai
half.blurb: Right across the border gate, a breezy coastal city known for parks, beaches and seaside promenades.

half.name: Chimelong Ocean Kingdom
half.blurb: One of the world's largest marine theme parks, packed with aquariums, rides and animal shows.

half.name: Guangzhou
half.blurb: A historic trading metropolis famed for its Cantonese food, temples and riverside city views.

half.name: Lantau Island
half.blurb: Reached across the delta bridge for the giant Big Buddha, cable car and old Tai O village.

half.name: Shenzhen
half.blurb: A modern boomtown people visit for its theme parks, huge malls and tech-driven city buzz.
